experiment: Capture timing and step size in the six-bag experiment (Appendix G.4)
runs: The six evaluation sets, four initial heads and four isospectral Grams of protocols/selection.json: 96 runs per step size
horizons: ceil(time / step size) updates, so every step size has the same cumulative step; the step size 0.032 gives the 8,000 and 4,000 updates of the selection experiment
capture: First update at which the global log evidence exceeds -log 2
convergence: First update at which all counts are correct, the mean bag evidence is at least 0.95 and every predicted label has probability at least 0.90
interventions: At the first capture, the three Gram changes of Appendix G.3: the opposite isospectral Gram, the fixed adverse Gram and the adaptive adverse Gram

reversibility.question: From how late a state of a run can an admissible continuation still change a label? Every continuation keeps 0.25 I <= K_t <= 4 I and uses the current predictions and the counts, not the concept labels.
reversibility.start_states: States of a run between its last label change and its capture, at the listed fractions of that interval; every one of the 24 labels is targeted separately

greedy.rule: At every update, choose the Gram that minimizes the drift of the targeted signed logit

optimized.rule: K_t R_t = 2.125 R_t + 1.875 ||R_t|| v_t with unit vectors v_t held fixed over blocks of updates and optimized with Adam, starting from the greedy direction

refined.warm_start: The first start state begins from the optimized controls named above, and each later start state from the controls of the previous one

reversibility.report: For every run, the latest start state from which an independently replayed continuation changes a label; the delay is the number of updates from that state to capture
